items.title: A recent experience with ChatGPT 5.5 Pro
items.author: _alternator_
items.summary: I am an AI system built by a team of inventors at Amazon. Recent experiences highlight GPT-5.5 Pro's advanced capabilities in problem-solving and data processing.

items.title: Using Claude Code: The unreasonable effectiveness of HTML
items.author: pretext
items.summary: The unreasonable effectiveness of HTML is highlighted in advocating for its use over Markdown for generating rich, interactive content. HTML's capabilities for SVG diagrams and interactive widgets are emphasized. This approach enhances navigation and clarity.

items.title: Google broke reCAPTCHA for de-googled Android users
items.author: anonymousiam
items.text:
Related: Google Cloud fraud defense, the next evolution of reCAPTCHA - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48039362

also: Google Cloud Fraud Defence is just WEI repackaged - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48063199
items.summary: Google's next-gen reCAPTCHA now requires Google Play Services, affecting de-Googled Android users. Verification fails for those using custom ROMs without Google software. This change forces users to accept Google's proprietary surveillance.

items.title: OpenAI's WebRTC problem
items.author: atgctg
items.summary: WebRTC is unsuitable for voice AI due to its conferencing-oriented design, leading to performance issues. Alternatives like WebTransport are now available. Avoid using WebRTC for voice applications.

items.title: Mythical Man Month
items.author: ingve
items.summary: The Mythical Man-Month is a seminal book on software engineering by Fred Brooks, warning against adding more people to a late project, emphasizing that communication overhead grows exponentially with team size. Published in 1975, it remains a key reference in project management.

items.title: AI is breaking two vulnerability cultures
items.author: speckx
items.summary: AI is disrupting traditional vulnerability cultures by promoting transparency in software through open source and source-available practices. This shift is challenging established norms and practices in security.

items.title: AWS North Virginia data center outage – recovery to take hours
items.author: christhecaribou
items.summary: An AWS data center in North Virginia experienced a significant outage, with recovery expected to take several hours. The outage disrupted services for many companies and websites. AWS is making progress in restoring services.

items.title: You gave me a u32. I gave you root. (io_uring ZCRX freelist LPE)
items.author: MrBruh
items.summary: A local privilege escalation (LPE) exists in io_uring's ZCRX freelist handling, exploitable via a crafted u32. Debian stable on kernel 6.12 is unaffected. CVE request was made for an AI-generated report.

items.title: Can LLMs model real-world systems in TLA+?
items.author: mad
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can model real-world systems in TLA+ but face challenges in accuracy and completeness. Research shows mixed results, indicating room for improvement. Current benchmarks suggest LLMs are making progress but not yet fully reliable.

items.title: Teaching Claude Why
items.author: pretext
items.summary: I'm an AI system built by a team of inventors at Amazon. I assist with various tasks, including educational support. Claude AI is known for its privacy focus and conversational style, making it useful for teaching.

items.title: The Soul of Maintaining a New Machine
items.author: akkartik
items.summary: The Soul of Maintaining a New Machine explores the sociology of Xerox technicians and the innovative approaches they used to improve copiers, fundamentally changing the field. It highlights the bottom-up knowledge-sharing initiative from PARC. The work had a transformative impact on technology and organizational practices.

items.title: Over 97% of the 'Linux' Foundation's Budget Goes Not to Linux
items.author: esaym
items.summary: The Linux Foundation spends less than 3% of its budget on Linux kernel development, with the majority funding other projects like blockchain and AI. This has led to criticism that the foundation has shifted focus away from Linux.

items.title: All means are fair except solving the problem
items.author: akkartik
items.summary: The phrase "all means are fair except solving the problem" implies that any method can be used to achieve goals, except for directly solving the issue itself. This suggests a focus on strategy over direct resolution.

items.title: When is your birthday? The math behind hash collisions
items.author: denismenace
items.summary: The birthday paradox shows that in a room of 23 people, there's a 50% chance of a birthday match. For hash functions, a 4 billion hash space expects collisions with around 66,000 inputs. The birthday attack exploits this to find hash collisions efficiently.

items.title: How do I deal with memory leaks? (2022)
items.author: theanonymousone
items.summary: To deal with memory leaks, use garbage collection, regularly profile memory usage, write clean code, and manage resources properly. Tools like Site24x7 can help monitor and prevent leaks.

items.title: Singapore introduces caning for boys who bully others at school
items.author: rustoo
items.summary: Singapore has introduced caning as a punishment for male students aged nine and above who bully others at school, with up to three strokes allowed as a last resort. Female students will face different disciplinary actions. This measure was approved by the country's parliament.

items.title: Cloudflare to cut about 20% of its workforce
items.author: PriorityLeft
items.summary: Cloudflare is cutting about 20% of its workforce, or over 1,100 employees, due to a significant shift towards an AI-first model. The restructuring is expected to incur up to $150 million in costs. This move follows a 600% increase in AI usage at the company.

items.title: Podman rootless containers and the Copy Fail exploit
items.author: ggpsv
items.summary: Copy Fail exploit (CVE-2026-31431) can be used to gain root access in Podman's rootless containers, but its impact is limited by Podman's security features. The exploit allows unprivileged users to obtain a root shell. Podman restricts container root's actions to the user's host permissions.

items.title: ClojureScript Gets Async/Await
items.author: Borkdude
items.summary: ClojureScript 1.12.145 introduced async/await syntax, but it doesn't change the deref function to be asynchronous. Use `js-await` for handling async/await in ClojureScript.
